title: The Loose Ghost
premise: Sebastian Halloran, a financial-crimes investigator who once worked a covert program called Loose Ghost, receives a meeting invitation from his dead handler, Mara Voss. Following it, he discovers the program never ended — it was absorbed by the very laundering network it was built to infiltrate, and its surviving operatives are being systematically erased. Hunted by both the network and the agency that disavowed him, Sebastian must reconstruct Voss's hidden ledger and burn the operation from the inside. In the end he trades his own clean record for the truth, exposing the network at devastating personal cost and walking away as a ghost himself.
about_author: August Montrose is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through offshore structures before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to outlast them.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Buried in routine SAR filings, he receives a calendar invite from Mara Voss — dead eleven months — for tomorrow, 9 p.m., a marina bar in Baltimore. He verifies her death certificate twice. The beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; he decides to go.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, flashback-laced. At work, his supervisor buries his flag on a shell company tied to a defense contractor. We learn of Loose Ghost: an off-book unit that taught him to think like a launderer, then dissolved. Beat: quiet rage at rules rewritten above his head.

chapters.title: Dead Man Talking
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the marina, no Voss — instead a burner phone taped under a table with a message in her cipher and a photo of him taken today. Someone is watching. He follows the cipher to a storage unit. Beat: paranoia becoming purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The unit holds Voss's half-finished ledger: fourteen accounts, one name redacted, and evidence that Loose Ghost's methods were sold to the network they once hunted. A car follows him home. Beat: the past is not past.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren Okafor's POV introduced. A former Loose Ghost analyst now working private security, Wren gets a termination order with Sebastian's name on it — and hesitates. She owed Voss. Beat: conscience versus contract.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren warns Sebastian off instead of killing him; he convinces her to look at the ledger. Together they identify three of the fourteen accounts. Beat: wary alliance, two ghosts recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Handler's Ghost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She reveals how Voss really died — officially a heart attack, but she'd scheduled a meeting with Wren the next day too. Voss knew she was marked. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Fourteen Doors
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Using old tradecraft, he maps the network's structure: a laundering architecture called the Cathedral, run by someone inside government oversight itself. The redacted name begins to resolve. Beat: vertigo at the scale of corruption.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. His agency suspends him, citing 'unauthorized contact with legacy personnel' — someone upstairs is protecting the Cathedral. His badge stops working mid-sentence. Beat: the system he served turns on him.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She stashes Sebastian in a decommissioned Loose Ghost safehouse; they decrypt more of Voss's files and find recordings — training tapes of themselves, kept as leverage. Beat: intimacy born of shared violation.

chapters.title: The Second Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The redacted name resolves: Deputy Director Alan Reeve, the man who signed off on Loose Ghost's dissolution — and its resale. Wren wants to go to the press; Sebastian insists they need the ledger complete first. Beat: first fracture between them.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To draw out the network's enforcer, Codex, they stage a fake handoff using Voss's cipher. It works too well — Codex takes the bait and nearly takes Wren. Beat: survival bought with blood and luck.

chapters.title: What Voss Knew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A final encrypted file plays: Voss explaining she leaked the invitation chain deliberately, choosing Sebastian because he still believed in the rules — the only kind of person who could burn the Cathedral credibly. Beat: devastating inheritance of trust.

chapters.title: Codex
chapters.summary: Codex's POV, unnamed until now. A former Loose Ghost operative who chose the money, he reports to Reeve that Sebastian has the ledger — and requests permission to use the old interrogation protocols. Beat: cold professionalism hiding a grudge.

chapters.title: The Cathedral's Heart
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following the money physically, they reach the network's operational hub in Wilmington — a compliance firm that launders for cartels and contractors alike. Sebastian walks in wearing his old suspended-badge authority. Beat: audacity as armor.

chapters.title: Inside the Machine
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Inside, he copies the master routing tables but trips a silent alarm. Wren extracts him under fire; the ledger is 90% complete but their faces are now in the system. Beat: victory curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV. He offers Sebastian reinstatement, a promotion, and silence — the same deal Voss refused. Sebastian records it. Beat: temptation rendered precisely, and refused.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Codex finds the safehouse. Wren holds him off long enough for Sebastian to escape with the ledger, taking a knife wound doing it. Beat: sacrifice, and the alliance sealed in cost.

chapters.title: The Distribution
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. From a hotel room, he executes Voss's plan: the full ledger goes simultaneously to a federal judge, three journalists, and every account holder on the list — including Reeve. No negotiation possible. Beat: the point of no return, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Arrests cascade; Reeve burns files and runs; Codex is ordered to erase everyone, starting with Wren. Sebastian goes back for her against all sense. Beat: chaos, loyalty over strategy.

chapters.title: Loose Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Confrontation at the marina where it began: Sebastian and Wren vs. Codex, ending with Codex dead by his own employers' cleanup crew — proof the network eats its own. Reeve is arrested on camera. Beat: catharsis without triumph.

chapters.title: After the Audit
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue. Testifying under immunity, he watches the Cathedral dismantled while knowing the machine will regrow elsewhere. He declines reinstatement, keeps Voss's cipher as a memento, and disappears — a loose ghost, finally free. Beat: bittersweet peace, justice outside the law at its true price.
